Adjusted assessment using SLOOS:
- Core message: The Fed notes stronger activity and a tight labor market but is focused on elevated inflation and geopolitical/supply-chain shocks, accompanying a faster tightening path (75 bp hike to 1.50–1.75% and balance sheet runoff).
- SLOOS overlay (Q1 2022): Banks on net eased standards for C&I loans and multifamily CRE; demand strengthened for C&I (including inventory, A/R, plant and equipment financing) and for most CRE; banks reduced the cost of credit lines. Household credit showed weaker demand for most RRE but stronger demand for HELOCs and auto loans, with eased standards for credit cards. Foreign banks tightened C&I standards.
- Implication: Domestic bank credit supply remained accommodative and demand was firm, indicating financial conditions through the banking channel were not yet restrictive. This cushions near-term growth relative to the FSR’s risk emphasis, but also validates the Fed’s hawkish stance to cool demand. Net tone remains negative given inflation and policy tightening, but less so than an FSR-only read.
